frameworks.name: Simple Instruction Prompting
frameworks.description: Direct natural-language instructions telling the model what to do.
weaknesses: May be incomplete for complex tasks
frameworks.example: Summarize the following paragraph in one sentence.

frameworks.name: Role-Based Prompting
frameworks.description: Prefix instructions with a role/persona (e.g., 'You are an expert historian').
frameworks.example: You are a friendly customer support agent. Answer the question below.

frameworks.name: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting (few-shot)
frameworks.description: Demonstrate step-by-step reasoning by providing one or more examples.
frameworks.example: Provide worked examples of arithmetic problems showing each step.

frameworks.name: Instruction Templating / Prompt Engineering Patterns
frameworks.description: Reusable templates with placeholders for task, input, constraints.

frameworks.name: Instruction Chaining / Decomposition Prompts
frameworks.description: Break complex tasks into sub-tasks executed sequentially.
frameworks.example: Decompose research and write a report into (1) find sources, (2) extract facts, (3) outline, (4) write.

frameworks.name: Self-Consistency (with CoT)
frameworks.description: Run multiple CoT generations and aggregate final answers to reduce errors.

frameworks.name: Zero-shot & One-shot Prompting
frameworks.description: No examples (zero-shot) or a single example (one-shot) with instruction.
weaknesses: Lower performance than few-shot for complex tasks

frameworks.name: Few-Shot Prompting (Classic)
frameworks.description: Provide several input-output examples showing desired mapping.

frameworks.name: Example Selection / Retrieval-Augmented Example Selection
frameworks.description: Use similarity search to pick most relevant few-shot examples.

frameworks.name: In-Context Learning Optimization (Automated Example Selection)
frameworks.description: Optimize which examples to include via evaluation-driven selection.
strengths: Near fine-tuning performance without weight updates

frameworks.name: Meta-Prompting / Example Synthesis
frameworks.description: Generate synthetic examples to expand few-shot set.
strengths: Useful when labeled data is scarce
weaknesses: Risk of bias or noise from synthetic data

frameworks.name: Stepwise Instruction (explicit steps)
frameworks.description: Ask the model to produce steps explicitly.

frameworks.name: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting (zero/few-shot)
frameworks.description: Encourage step-by-step reasoning via instructions or examples.
weaknesses: Reliability varies across models and tasks

frameworks.name: Program-of-Thoughts / Tree-of-Thoughts (conceptual)
frameworks.description: Encourage branching reasoning trajectories before selecting an answer.
weaknesses: Hard to implement purely in prompt

frameworks.name: Tree of Thoughts (ToT) (implemented)
frameworks.description: Search-based approach: generate candidate reasoning steps, expand branches, prune/backtrack.
weaknesses: Needs external controller and many calls

frameworks.name: Programmatic Reasoning (LLM + External Execution)
frameworks.description: Generate code/symbolic steps executed by a runtime (calculator, interpreter).

frameworks.name: Contextual Retrieval (manual)
frameworks.description: Append retrieved context (documents/facts) to the prompt.

frameworks.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
frameworks.description: Retrieve relevant passages then condition generation on those passages.

frameworks.name: Citation and Attribution Prompts
frameworks.description: Instruct the model to cite retrieved passages or provide sources inline.

frameworks.name: Closed-Loop Retrieval (Retriever-Generator Feedback)
frameworks.description: Iteratively refine retrieval with generator feedback until confidence threshold.

frameworks.name: Retrieval + Reasoning Hybrid (RAG + CoT)
frameworks.description: Combine retrieval with chain-of-thought reasoning using evidence.
strengths: Handles complex queries requiring facts and reasoning

frameworks.name: Tool-Call Prompts (explicit)
frameworks.description: Instruct the model when and how to call external tools; orchestration is manual.
weaknesses: Requires external code for tool invocation and handling

frameworks.name: ReAct (Reasoning + Acting)
frameworks.description: Interleave reasoning traces with explicit actions and observations.

frameworks.name: Toolformer / Self-supervised Tool-Use
frameworks.description: Train or prompt LLMs to decide when to call tools via self-supervised signals.
weaknesses: Often requires fine-tuning or specialized prompts

frameworks.name: Agent Frameworks / Multi-Agent Orchestration
frameworks.description: Multiple agents coordinate, call tools, and negotiate responsibilities.

frameworks.name: Prompt Calibration (temperature, instructions)
frameworks.description: Adjust generation parameters and explicit constraints for determinism.
weaknesses: Limited ability to fix logical errors

frameworks.name: Prompt Tuning (soft prompts) — Interface-level
frameworks.description: Use continuous prompt vectors optimized via gradients without weight updates.

frameworks.name: Prefix Tuning / Adapter Prompts
frameworks.description: Train small prefix layers or adapters that steer model behavior.
weaknesses: Requires more infra and model access

frameworks.name: Prompt Engineering + Fine-Tuning Hybrid
frameworks.description: Combine prompt design with (few-shot/full) fine-tuning for best performance.

frameworks.name: Automatic Prompt Optimization (APO)
frameworks.description: Algorithmic search over prompts to maximize task metrics.

frameworks.name: Output Constraints and Templates
frameworks.description: Force output formats via explicit instructions and examples.

frameworks.name: Red-Teaming Prompting (manual)
frameworks.description: Adversarial prompts to probe model failure modes.

frameworks.name: Self-Evaluation / Chain-of-Thought Verification
frameworks.description: Ask the model to critique, verify, or rate its own answer.

frameworks.name: Contrastive & Counterfactual Prompting
frameworks.description: Generate counterfactual answers or compare options to detect inconsistencies.

frameworks.name: Ensemble & Cross-Checking Prompts
frameworks.description: Use multiple LLMs or prompt styles and reconcile outputs via a verifier.

frameworks.name: Formal Verification via LLMs + Symbolic Tools
frameworks.description: Combine LLM outputs with symbolic verification (type checkers, unit tests).

frameworks.name: Style & Tone Prompts
frameworks.description: Provide explicit style guides or examples to shape voice.

frameworks.name: Iterative Refinement / Revision Prompts
frameworks.description: Produce a draft, then request revisions with specific feedback.

frameworks.name: Prompted Template Filling (story skeletons)
frameworks.description: Provide narrative scaffolds and ask the model to fill in scenes.
weaknesses: May produce clichés if scaffolding is narrow

frameworks.name: Co-Creation & Collaborative Prompts
frameworks.description: Define roles for model and human for iterative collaboration with checkpoints.
strengths: Powerful for creative teams and large projects

frameworks.name: Prompting for Multimodal Models
frameworks.description: Include or reference images, audio, or video with instructions.

frameworks.name: Few-Shot Program Synthesis Prompts
frameworks.description: Provide code input-output pairs to synthesize similar code.
weaknesses: Risk of insecure code and subtle bugs

frameworks.name: Latent Space Steering & Activation Engineering
frameworks.description: Manipulate internal activations to produce desired behaviors.

frameworks.name: Instruction Distillation & Modular Persona Composition
frameworks.description: Distill large instruction sets into compact modules and compose them.
weaknesses: Requires systematic module design and testing

frameworks.name: Prompt-as-Policy (for RL/Decision tasks)
frameworks.description: Treat prompts as policies optimized via RL or policy gradient.
strengths: Formal framework for optimizing interactive prompts

notes.coverage: Emphasizes widely used frameworks as of late 2025; not exhaustive.
bestPractices: Start simple, iterate with few-shot, CoT, and retrieval
Keep prompts small and modular; orchestrate multi-step flows
